### Problem: Registration system {#sec-cx-p6-registration}

::: {.p-statement}
Process $n \le 10^5$ registration requests, each a name of up to 32 lowercase letters. If the name is new, register it and print `OK`. Otherwise print `name` followed by the smallest $i \ge 1$ such that `name`$i$ is not registered yet, and register that.

Source: [CF 4C · Registration System](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/4/C){.solved rating="1300"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Names contain only letters, so a generated `name`$i$ can never equal a requested name. For each base name the suffixes are therefore handed out as 1, 2, 3, … in order, so a counter per name is enough. A dictionary makes each request $O(L)$ to hash a name of length $L$.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **List-based.** Keep a list of taken names and test `candidate in taken`, trying $i = 1, 2, \dots$. Each test is $O(nL)$, and a name requested $n$ times tries up to $n$ suffixes: $O(n^3 L)$ in the worst case. Even the simpler "count occurrences in a list" version is $O(n^2 L)$.
2. **Dictionary counter.** `cnt[name]` = number of times seen. If 0, print `OK`; else print `name + str(cnt[name])`. Then increment. $O(nL)$ expected.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
#### Python

```{python}
#| label: cx-registration
def registration(names):
    cnt, out = {}, []
    for s in names:
        c = cnt.get(s, 0)
        out.append("OK" if c == 0 else f"{s}{c}")
        cnt[s] = c + 1
    return out

def registration_list(names):
    taken, out, ops = [], [], 0
    for s in names:
        cand, i = s, 0
        while True:
            ops += len(taken)                       # cost of `cand in taken`
            if cand not in taken:
                break
            i += 1
            cand = f"{s}{i}"
        taken.append(cand)
        out.append("OK" if i == 0 else cand)
    return out, ops

for _ in range(300):
    names = [random.choice(["a", "b", "ab", "abc"]) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 25))]
    assert registration(names) == registration_list(names)[0]

assert registration(["abacaba", "acaba", "abacaba", "acab"]) == ["OK", "OK", "abacaba1", "OK"]
assert registration(["first", "first", "second", "second", "third", "third"]) == \
    ["OK", "first1", "OK", "second1", "OK", "third1"]
_, ops = registration_list(["x"] * 300)
print("list version, 300 equal names:", ops, "membership comparisons")
assert ops > 300**3 / 10
```

#### C++

```cpp
int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n; cin >> n;
    unordered_map<string, int> cnt;
    while (n--) {
        string s; cin >> s;
        int& c = cnt[s];
        if (c == 0) cout << "OK\n";
        else cout << s << c << '\n';
        ++c;
    }
}
```
:::

::: {#fig-cx-registration}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
ns = list(range(20, 201, 20))
list_ops = [registration_list(["x"] * k)[1] for k in ns]
assert all(b > a for a, b in zip(list_ops, list_ops[1:]))
def reg(ax, p):
    ax.plot(ns, list_ops, "o-", color=p["red"], lw=2, label="list: `cand in taken`")
    ax.plot(ns, ns, "o-", color=p["green"], lw=2, label="dict: one lookup per request")
    ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_xlabel("number of requests n (all the same name)")
    ax.set_ylabel("comparisons"); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
V.plot(reg)
```

Membership comparisons for n equal names: the list version grows like n³ (each of up to n suffixes is tested against a list of up to n names); the dictionary does one O(1) lookup per request.

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Time** $O(nL)$ expected with a hash map ($O(nL\log n)$ with `std::map`). **Space** $O(nL)$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The counter shortcut relies on names having no digits; with digits allowed, `a1` could be both a request and a generated name, and you would need to check the dictionary in a loop.
- Hash maps on adversarial inputs: on Codeforces, tests can be built to make `unordered_map` with the default hash degrade to $O(n)$ per operation. Use a randomised custom hash, or `std::map`.
- Use `'\n'` and fast I/O for $10^5$ output lines.
:::
